title: Migration Planning: Assessment, Strategies, Dependencies, and Licensing
bodyMarkdown:
## The migration journey

Google frames migration in phases: **Assess → Plan → Migrate (deploy) → Optimize**. Most planning failures happen because teams skip a rigorous assessment.

### Assess with Migration Center

**Migration Center** is the unified tool for the assessment phase. It:

- Discovers on-prem and cloud assets (servers, VMs, databases).
- Maps **application dependencies** (what talks to what) so you can group apps into migration *waves* and avoid breaking integrations.
- Recommends **right-sized** Google Cloud machine types.
- Produces **TCO / cost estimates** for the business case.

Good assessment data feeds your KPIs, ROI model, and wave plan.

## The migration strategies (the "R"s)

| Strategy | What you do | Effort | When |
|----------|-------------|--------|------|
| **Rehost** (lift & shift) | Move as-is, VM-to-VM | low | Tight deadline; modernize later |
| **Replatform** (move & improve) | Minor cloud optimizations (e.g., self-managed DB → Cloud SQL) | medium | Quick wins available |
| **Refactor / re-architect** | Redesign for cloud-native (containers, serverless) | high | Long-term agility/scale matters |
| **Repurchase** | Replace with SaaS | varies | Commodity capability exists |
| **Retire** | Decommission | low | App no longer needed |
| **Retain** | Keep where it is (for now) | none | Not yet ready / constrained |

The build/buy/modify/deprecate lens maps onto these: prefer **buy/repurchase** for commodity functions, **retire** redundant apps, and **refactor** only where it earns its keep.

## Dependency and network planning

- Build a dependency map before sequencing waves — co-migrate tightly coupled apps.
- Plan **non-overlapping IP ranges** between on-prem and Google Cloud VPCs early.
- Choose hybrid connectivity: **Cloud VPN** (lower bandwidth, quick) or **Cloud Interconnect** (Dedicated/Partner, high bandwidth, low latency) for data transfer and cutover.
- For large datasets, plan the **data movement** method: online (Storage Transfer Service, Database Migration Service, Datastream) vs offline (**Transfer Appliance**) when network transfer would take too long.

## Licensing planning

Licensing is a real TCO driver — don't ignore it.

- **Pay-as-you-go (license-included) images** for Windows Server / SQL Server bundle licensing into the hourly rate; simplest for new deployments and compliant by default.
- **Bring Your Own License (BYOL):** reuse eligible existing licenses. When a license requires **dedicated physical hardware**, use **sole-tenant nodes** to satisfy compliance.
- Model license cost across the steady-state fleet (including autoscaling) in your TCO — autoscaled PAYG instances are billed per instance-hour, not "repurchased."

## Cutover and validation

1. Migrate in waves; validate functionality and NFRs (latency, throughput) against baselines.
2. Keep rollback options until confidence is high.
3. Optimize post-migration: right-size, apply CUDs/Spot where appropriate, adopt managed services.
